summary: Reviewed logs, diagnostics, HTTP behavior, and persisted state on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 musl host (http://127.0.0.1:8096, prefix /tmp/jf) for secret leakage and unbounded data, using the committed mock Sonarr/Radarr fixture and real webhook deliveries with distinctive sentinel secrets. Negative result: no credential leaked outside the accepted Jellyfin plugin configuration, and no unbounded path was found, so no production code was changed. Evidence: (1) Secret leakage - sentinels SONARR-SENTINEL-KEY-1b8d4f6a-DO-NOT-LEAK, RADARR-SENTINEL-KEY-7f3a9c2e-DO-NOT-LEAK, WEBHOOK-SENTINEL-SECRET-9e2c7a5d-DO-NOT-LEAK, and a wrong WRONG-SONARR-SENTINEL-KEY-aaaa1111-DO-NOT-LEAK were used across provider success, 401 auth failure, malformed response, oversized response, request timeout, and webhook success/missing/wrong/oversized/malformed paths. A whole-host case-sensitive literal search of /tmp/jf/data, /tmp/jf/config, /tmp/jf/cache, /tmp/jf/log, /tmp/jf/console.log found each sentinel in exactly one file - the Jellyfin plugin configuration data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml, which ADR-005 designates as the single source of truth - and nowhere in the console log, the log directory, the plugin state, the installed plugin folder, or the mock request log. No X-Api-Key/Authorization header value, connection credential, or exception text carrying a secret appeared anywhere. The plugin assembly contains no logging call at all; SecretLease (ToString omits the value, value cleared on Dispose), ArrProviderError (512-char bounded/redacted message) and ArtworkOperationErrors (512-char bounded, control-free) enforce the redaction/bounding contract. (2) Persisted state - the state root /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags contained metadata-state, artwork-operation, published artwork-state, and content-addressed source-artifact records, all written as versioned envelopes (SchemaVersion, Kind, RecordId, Authority, Terminal, UpdatedUtc) with a SHA-256 PayloadSha256 integrity tag and traversal-safe single-segment identifiers (PluginStatePaths rejects '..', rooted paths, and invalid filename characters). Records contained only item ids, connection-scoped provider identity, provider/decimal/hash fingerprints, image tags, timestamps, and state enums; no secret. The only URL present was the non-secret configured provider base URL (http://127.0.0.1:7878 / http://127.0.0.1:8989) inside the metadata-state cache key, which is by design and contains no credential. (3) HTTP behavior - the two anonymous POST routes /ArrTags/Webhook/{Sonarr,Radarr} authenticated only through the X-ArrTags-Webhook-Secret header via the constant-time versioned ADR-005 lease and returned uniform, non-reflecting outcomes: 401 for missing, wrong, and >1024-char candidates; 413 (Content Too Large) for both a declared 300,000-byte body and a chunked 300,000-byte body (bound enforced before allocation); 400 for malformed JSON, wrong shape, and empty body; 202/null for valid deliveries. The plugin exposes no other route (only ArrTagsWebhookController) and registers no middleware, so the standard image route authorization remains Jellyfin's own (anonymous GET /Items/{id}/Images/Primary returned 200 for both items). (4) Bounded data - every ADR-004/ADR-012 operational bound was confirmed to have an explicit value enforced at its boundary, not merely validated at config load: queue capacity 512 (LibraryWorkQueue drops/coalesces overflow), per-item single-flight 1, provider concurrency per-connection/global 4/8 via DynamicConcurrencyLimiter, render concurrency 2, HTTP timeout 15s, transient retries 2 with bounded exponential backoff (max 15s) at both the provider and worker boundaries, provider response size 8 MiB checked by Content-Length and while streaming, webhook payload 256 KiB, source/derived artifact 32 MiB, decoded image dimension 8192/side, reconciliation batch 100, metadata last-known-good window 24h (total, fresh half + stale half), render cache TTL 24h/quota 1 GiB, authoritative artifact quota 4 GiB (rejects new derived work on exhaustion), and terminal-provenance retention 30 days. A hosted StateRetentionService applies cache/quota, metadata-freshness, terminal-provenance, and artifact-GC retention hourly (first pass immediately) in production; WebhookIntake is bounded at 256 with a 4x coalescing window; webhook episode entries are capped at 32 and JSON depth at 16; WebhookReconciliationResolver bounds work to ReconciliationBatchSize; diagnostic/diagnostic text is capped at 512 characters. Documentation updated: PLANS.md (task 7.4 checkbox, a Task 7.4 status paragraph, Project Status line, Milestone 7 row), docs/changelog.md (Phase 7 status + a task 7.4 section), README.md and docs/implementation-readiness.md status lines. No product test was added because the review found no defect and the existing redaction/retention/boundary tests already cover the contract.

Focused contract run: `dotnet test ArrTags.slnx -c Release --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SecretBoundaryTests|FullyQualifiedName~ProviderFailureMatrixTests|FullyQualifiedName~WebhookResolutionTests|FullyQualifiedName~ArtifactRetentionTests|FullyQualifiedName~StateBoundaryTests|FullyQualifiedName~MetadataStateStoreTests|FullyQualifiedName~ConfigurationFoundationTests"` -> Failed 0, Passed 145, Skipped 0, Total 145.

Live plugin install/load: package extracted to /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0, host restarted via scripts/provision-jellyfin-test-host.sh /tmp/jf; console logged 'Loaded assembly ArrTags, Version=0.1.0.0 ...' and 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.0'.

Live provider traffic (committed mock fixture scripts/mock-arr-fixture.cs + scripts/mock-arr-fixtures, started with ARRTAGS_MOCK_RADARR_KEY=RADARR-SENTINEL-KEY-7f3a9c2e-DO-NOT-LEAK and ARRTAGS_MOCK_SONARR_KEY=SONARR-SENTINEL-KEY-1b8d4f6a-DO-NOT-LEAK): real Jellyfin Movie and Series/Episode with local .nfo provider ids (Tmdb 990001 / Imdb tt9900001, Tvdb 990002 series / Tvdb 990004 episode) and local poster JPEGs, libraries added via POST /Library/VirtualFolders, reconciliation via POST /ScheduledTasks/Running/0e96fc3004bcd22db45dd641e63e2666 -> 204; the mock logged provider=radarr/sonarr GET /api/v3/movie, /api/v3/moviefile?movieId=1, /api/v3/series, /api/v3/episode?seriesId=1&includeEpisodeFile=true, /api/v3/episodeFile?seriesId=1 with apiKey=valid status=200; the plugin persisted matched metadata state and published artwork state for both items.

Live secret scan (case-sensitive literal value search): `grep -rIl -F <sentinel> /tmp/jf/console.log /tmp/jf/log /tmp/jf/data /tmp/jf/config /tmp/jf/cache` for SONARR-SENTINEL-KEY-1b8d4f6a-DO-NOT-LEAK, RADARR-SENTINEL-KEY-7f3a9c2e-DO-NOT-LEAK, WEBHOOK-SENTINEL-SECRET-9e2c7a5d-DO-NOT-LEAK, and WRONG-SONARR-SENTINEL-KEY-aaaa1111-DO-NOT-LEAK -> each of the three configured sentinels matched only /tmp/jf/data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml (the ADR-005 source of truth); the wrong sentinel matched no host file, and no sentinel matched /tmp/jf/console.log, /tmp/jf/log, /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags, /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0, or the mock request log.

Live provider failure paths (real provider clients, sentinel secrets in use): auth failure - Sonarr configured with a wrong key, mock returned 401, mock log 'apiKey=invalid status=401'; timeout - Radarr base URL pointed at the non-routable http://10.255.255.1:7878 with RequestTimeoutSeconds=2, producing a real request timeout; malformed response - instrumented sonarr/series.json served '{ "this is": not valid json' (200 body); oversized response - instrumented radarr/movies.json served 10,000,000 bytes (200 body, above the 8 MiB provider-response limit). After each path the sentinel scan above still found no sentinel in logs/state, and the movie metadata-state was retained as explicit stale last-known-good (State=1) with LastError=null rather than being replaced by unvalidated data.

Live webhook traffic and HTTP bounds: `curl -X POST /ArrTags/Webhook/Sonarr|Radarr -H 'X-ArrTags-Webhook-Secret: <secret>'` -> valid 202 (null body); missing secret -> 401 (RFC9110 problem+json with only type/title/status/traceId); wrong secret -> 401; >1024-char candidate -> 401; 300,000-byte body with Content-Length -> 413; 300,000-byte chunked body -> 413; malformed JSON -> 400; wrong shape {"foo":"bar"} -> 400; empty body -> 400. No response echoed the secret, headers, bodies, or configuration detail.

Live persisted-state inventory: /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags contained cache/metadata-state/{movie-radarr,episode-sonarr}.json (2,992 and 2,857 bytes), authoritative/artwork-operation/{item}-Primary.json (terminal), authoritative/artwork-state/{item}-Primary.json, and authoritative/source-artifact/*.json plus artifacts/source/<shard>/*.bin (max 58,431 bytes observed). Every JSON record began with a versioned envelope (SchemaVersion:1, Kind, RecordId, Authority, Terminal, UpdatedUtc) and carried a PayloadSha256 SHA-256 integrity tag; no record contained api-key/webhook-secret/password material, and the only URL was the non-secret configured provider base URL.

Live standard image route and route inventory: anonymous `curl http://127.0.0.1:8096/Items/{id}/Images/Primary` -> HTTP 200 (image/jpeg 1,124 bytes and image/png 8,277 bytes) served by Jellyfin's own AuthorizationMiddleware/ImageController; source search for `[Route`/`[ApiController`/`ControllerBase`/middleware/MapX found only ArrTagsWebhookController with its two [HttpPost] actions, i.e. the plugin adds no image route and no authorization bypass.

Host left clean and running: removed the ArrTags install folder, plugin state, plugin configuration, and the ArrTagsMovies/ArrTagsTV virtual folders; deleted the recreated test media; stopped the mock fixture; restarted via the provision script -> grep counted 0 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags', 0 [ERR]/[FTL], 1 'Startup complete', GET /System/Info/Public -> 12.0.0, and /tmp/jf/data/ArrTags and /tmp/jf/data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml are absent.

`git status --short` -> only PLANS.md, README.md, docs/changelog.md, docs/implementation-readiness.md, and the new docs/implementation/7.4/worker-report.json; no source, test, fixture, or packaging file changed. /tmp/7.4 and /tmp/7.8 removed.
known_limitations: No secret leak or unbounded-data defect was found, so this task deliberately made no production change and added no regression test; the contract is covered by the existing 145 focused secret-boundary, provider-failure, webhook-resolution, state-boundary, metadata-state, artifact-retention, and configuration-foundation tests plus the full default and host-guarded suites.

There is no user-facing or plugin diagnostic/status surface (a documented Phase 7 deferral), so the 'diagnostics/status output' portion of the review covers the Jellyfin console log, the log directory, the scheduled-task outcome, the persisted plugin state, and the source, not a dedicated status endpoint.

No live Sonarr or Radarr instance is available in this environment; provider success and failure traffic was generated against the committed mock fixture (scripts/mock-arr-fixture.cs + scripts/mock-arr-fixtures/), so real-release payload variance and real TLS/HTTP-stack logging behavior are covered only by the ADR-013 contract fixtures and the pinned transport code.

The failing provider paths (401 auth failure, timeout, malformed, oversized) were exercised live, but the durable metadata-state records retained last-known-good metadata with LastError=null rather than persisting the redacted provider error text, so live evidence of redaction is the absence of any sentinel/header/exception leak in the logs and state plus the unit-level redaction assertions (ArrProviderError/ArtworkOperationErrors/SecretLease), not a persisted redacted error string.

Runtime configuration replacement is still not wired to Jellyfin's configuration-update mechanism (a documented Phase 7 deferral), so each configuration change required writing data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml and restarting the host; live in-process configuration replacement was not exercised.

The credentials are persisted in Jellyfin's plugin configuration XML data/plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml. This is the accepted ADR-005 contract (Jellyfin's configuration is the single V1 source of truth and protection at rest follows Jellyfin's data-folder permissions); the review confirms that this is the only host location containing them, not that the XML is secret-free.

The plugin carries the configured (non-secret) provider base URL in the metadata-state cache key and connection identity. This is intended and contains no credential; the connection identity strips user information, and no credential/header value was found in any state record.

The pinned host database still contains pre-existing orphaned library item rows from tasks 7.3/7.8 (their virtual-folder definitions, test media, plugin install, plugin state, and plugin configuration were removed and the host is running clean); this matches the state the previous verification left and is test-environment residue, not a product behavior.
